subject: Dedicated pool load shedding: customer communications & next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <priyanka@pinecone-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool load shedding - interim notice and immediate mitigations

Hi Priyanka / Derek —

I want to notify you about an event that started at ~09:00 UTC this morning impacting the dedicated GPU pool serving your account. We observed a sustained surge of inference traffic combined with an unexpected increase in long-sequence requests from a small subset of your workloads. The autoscaler reacted by prioritizing latency-sensitive requests, which resulted in proactive load-shedding of lower-priority background jobs.

Impact observed:
- Brief (<6 min) increase in 5xx and rate-limited requests for scheduled batch jobs (background tuning pipelines).
- Slight tail-latency increase for a small fraction (<2%) of interactive requests while we rerouted traffic.

Immediate actions we took (already in progress):
1) Emergency shard expansion to temporarily increase pool headroom.
2) Dynamic routing: we rerouted non-critical requests to a warm-standby cluster and downgraded a non-essential model variant to reduce peak throughput.
3) Load-shedding of scheduled background jobs to protect interactive SLOs.
4) On-call engineering is collecting detailed logs and a short artifact set (attached cluster-load-report.pdf).

Next steps we propose for transparency and remediation:
- Short incident call within the next 2 hours if you'd like a live walk-through (available at 11:30 UTC).
- Sharing full logs and a technical summary once we complete root-cause analysis.
- A proposed customer credit to offset any measurable job re-runs (we'll share a draft).

We recognize the disruption this causes and are prioritizing restoring steady-state capacity and preventing recurrence. I'll follow up with a technical note from our infra team with root-cause hypotheses. Apologies for the inconvenience — we appreciate your patience.

Attachments: cluster-load-report.pdf (summary)

Best,
So
Soojin Lee

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated pool load shedding - interim notice and immediate mitigations (technical notes)

Folks — quick technical summary from on-call infra:

Root cause (current hypothesis):
- The autoscaler saw a rapid rise in per-request memory pressure caused by several long-sequence generation requests (token counts ~3x usual).
- Our threshold evaluation loop runs at 15s granularity; when several noisy workers reported high KV cache growth simultaneously, the scaler triggered backfill prioritization to keep latency SLOs, which led to shedding of background job queues.
- A recent model-variant rollout (nonbreaking) changed request CPU/memory characteristics; we did not have the new sequence-length profile included in our autoscale heuristics.

Immediate fixes (next 24h):
1) Add a quick fix to prevent shedding of scheduled jobs until a minimum expansion has completed (hotfix queued).
2) Push a patch to autoscaler to account for request sequence-length percentiles before making eviction decisions.
3) Run a synthetic traffic job that mirrors Pinecone's sequence distribution (scheduled overnight) to validate.

Longer-term plan (2–3 weeks):
- Implement predictive scaling using rolling-window sequence-length forecasting.
- Improve deployment gating to ensure variant memory/throughput delta is tested against autoscaler heuristics.
- Schedule a capacity review with Pinecone to discuss committed headroom and burst buffer settings.

Attachments: cluster-logs.tar.gz (raw logs) — contains worker traces, scaler decisions, and timing.

I'll open RI-7654 for the software fix and link it to the incident runbook.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Priyanka Rao <priyanka@pinecone-analytics.com>, Derek Nguyen <derek@pinecone-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 01 Aug 2027 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Follow-up: load-shedding incident – summary, remedies, and customer action items

Hi Priyanka / Derek —

Thanks again for joining the call yesterday. Below is a concise summary, our deliverables, and timelines so you have a single place to track next steps.

What happened (summary):
- A combination of an unexpected shift in request sequence-length distribution and our autoscaler heuristics caused prioritized scaling decisions that temporarily shed lower-priority batch jobs in your dedicated pool. No customer data was exfiltrated or corrupted; persisted job state is intact.

What we've done so far:
- Restored steady-state pool capacity and validated request latencies against your SLOs.
- Hotfix deployed to prevent immediate shedding of scheduled jobs until expansion completes.
- Collected logs and artifacts (attached).

Deliverables and timeline:
- Technical post-incident report (public summary + detailed appendix): Aug 10, 2027.
- Software fix for autoscaler heuristics (RI-7654): targeted rollout Aug 7, 2027.
- Nightly synthetic load test run to validate behavior: scheduled Aug 2–3, 2027.
- Capacity review / adjustment meeting (commitment discussion): propose week of Aug 9 — suggest Aug 11 at 17:00 UTC.
- Draft credit offer for measurable job re-runs: attached draft-credit-offer.pdf, please review and we can finalize by Aug 5.

Action items for Pinecone Analytics:
- Please confirm the specific job IDs you believe were impacted so we can correlate with our logs (Derek shared a short list on the call).
- Review draft-credit-offer.pdf and flag any questions by Aug 4 so finance can process.
- If acceptable, confirm the Aug 11 capacity review meeting date/time.

Internal notes: I'll link RI-7654 and the incident artifacts to the customer folder; Marissa will own the capacity review scheduling and Ben will coordinate the billing/credit flow.

Attachments: draft-credit-offer.pdf | cluster-load-report.pdf | cluster-logs.tar.gz
Links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RI-7654 | https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-redwood-incident-archives

Apologies again for the disruption. We're treating this as a high-priority reliability item and will keep you updated on the timeline above.

Best,
So
